title: Choose the visual world for Kimma.ai
question: The roll assigned The Reading Room. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Reading Room
options.lineage: archival reading rooms, catalog cards and finding aids
options.thesis: Your background handled like an archive: every claim catalogued with its provenance, every judgment cross-referenced to the moment it was said.
materials: catalog card stock with a red top rule
violet rubber-stamp ink for everything the AI marks
options.viewport: The desk: the CV at true page scale with a violet slip marker landing on the line being asked about, the question typed on a catalog card above it, a quiet violet stamp as the AI's presence, and a finding-aid outline of the phases at right.
options.risk: Archives can read dusty or slow beside a realtime AI, and card stock invites the cream-paper default; the grammar must live in details, never in the call controls.

raised.raise: Crouwel: the catalog card's ruled lines become the literal layout armature; every element snaps to one card-rule unit.
Saville: total numbering; every role, candidate, interview, claim, quote and rating carries its call number as its identity.
Timetable: dense surfaces (transcript, report, catalog) use one text size; rank comes from weight, case, reversal and rule.
Feed: exactly one document owns the desk at a time; switching documents is a hard swap, never tiles.
Specimen: live typewriter readouts (timecode, phase clock, page:line) are the only chrome that moves.

options.label: The Control Room
options.lineage: live broadcast control rooms and rundowns
options.thesis: The interview as a live produced segment: an ON AIR tally for honest recording, a rundown of phases, and timecode on every piece of evidence.
options.viewport: The program monitor shows the agent's screen, preview shows what's next, and the rundown runs down the side with the live segment lit.
options.risk: Near-black with a lit accent is a look many AI products already ship, and a studio can feel like being on trial to a nervous candidate.

options.label: Claim and Proof
options.thesis: Every rating sits beside the proof that earns it: near-black on near-white, one accent, a claim and then its quote.
options.viewport: A calm two-column room: the agent's screen on the left, captions and claim-proof pairs on the right, one accent for the live state.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: claim-then-proof is exactly evidence-linked scoring, and recruiters live in this look; holds audience identification and ties on clarity.
options.risk: It is how most AI recruiting tools already look, so Kimma.ai blends in with Metaview and Ashby.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Every screen built cell by cell on a visible construction grid.
options.viewport: A monumental grid-built headline over the candidate's record.
options.case: Fuses poorly: neither recruiters nor candidates identify with type-specimen posters, and a monumental grid fights a calm call.
options.kept: The card's ruled lines as the literal layout armature.
options.risk: Design-world spectacle that upstages the interview.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Every artifact gets a catalog number, and color codes stand in for words.
options.viewport: The interview's audio plotted as a stack of white lines with only its number as the headline.
options.case: Fuses poorly: coded labels hide meaning from anxious candidates and busy recruiters.
options.kept: Total numbering: every artifact carries its number as its identity.
options.risk: Mystique where the product needs plain clarity.

options.label: Timetable Rack
options.lineage: 1970s pocket airline timetables on a light table
options.thesis: One type size everywhere; rank carried by weight, case, reversal and rule.
options.viewport: Interview schedules as raked timetable slides.
options.case: Fuses poorly: raked containers and goldenrod glare cost a live call its clarity.
options.kept: One text size on dense surfaces; rank by weight, case, reversal and rule.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One item owns the entire viewport, the next one snap away.
options.viewport: Each claim full-screen, one snap at a time.
options.case: Fuses poorly: full-screen snapping fits neither a recruiter's scan nor a dense report.
options.kept: One document owns the desk at a time; switching is a hard swap.
options.risk: Entertainment grammar in a hiring decision.

options.label: Variable Specimen
options.thesis: Hierarchy by scale contrast alone, with a live readout of every value.
options.viewport: A giant letter that morphs as the conversation moves.
options.case: Fuses poorly: axis-morphing type has no job in an interview.
options.kept: Live mono readouts are the only moving chrome.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Clean AI-recruiting software with a Meet-style dark call stage, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A video-call stage with an AI tile and a side panel for captions and notes.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
